patch.value: Bare pm comments / pm notes reads keep the oldest page when output must be bounded, withholding the newest entries (GH-1605 fixed this for history only)

Measured on pm 2026.11.1 against this repository's tracker. When a bare read of an item's comments or notes has to be bounded, it returns the OLDEST page and withholds the newest entries:

- pm comments pm-7zs0 --json (261 comments) returns 28 entries dated 2026-06-10..2026-06-30 with has_more: true and an output cursor. The newest entry (2026-11-01) is reachable only through --limit N ("Return only latest n comments") or by following about ten cursors.
- pm notes pm-doxj --json returns 28 notes dated 2026-06-07..2026-07-10, while pm notes pm-doxj --limit 1 shows the newest note is from 2026-09-28.

This is the same defect GH-1605 (pm-gh1605) fixed for pm history: a default read should preserve the recent tail when it must truncate. The annotation surfaces did not get that fix. It has a real cost. While recording a release-health checkpoint, an agent verified its new comment with pm comments <id> --json | .comments[-1], saw a June entry, concluded the write had failed, and posted a duplicate that then had to be deleted with --delete. On long-lived living-map items, the newest evidence is exactly what the default view hides.

Scope: the default bounded selection for pm comments and pm notes (and pm learnings, if it shares the reader). Explicit --limit already selects the latest N.

A bare pm comments <id> and pm notes <id> read that must be bounded returns the newest entries (the recent tail) and reports the omitted older entries with a cursor that continues backwards; pm learnings follows the same rule; Regression test: an item with more annotations than the default bound returns the latest entry on a bare read in JSON and TOON; Command reference documents the bounded default for annotation reads
A bare annotation read on a long-lived item always includes the most recent comment or note.
pm comments pm-7zs0 --json returns 28 comments from June 2026 out of 261; the 2026-11-01 entry is withheld.

value.text: Duplicate-check evidence: the strict duplicate guard flagged pm-gh1605 (closed). Its title, AC and resolution are scoped to pm history only ('Preserve newest compact/provenance history...'), so reopening it would widen a shipped item. This item covers the sibling annotation readers that did not receive the same tail-preserving default. Related closed precedent: pm-6vfg (MCP pm_comments default limit). Searched: pm search 'comments default page oldest latest bounded read'.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Investigation and implementation (2026-11-07, branch fix/annotation-collection-reads). Root cause: the universal budget compaction (compactRowsToBudget in src/sdk/read-output-budget.ts) and the --output-limit bound (boundReadOutputRows in src/sdk/read-output-rows.ts) always retained the FIRST rows of a declared collection, while the annotation producer stores entries oldest first. So pm comments pm-7zs0 --json returned indexes 1..28 of 263, and --output-limit 2 returned the two oldest comments while --limit 2 returned the two newest. pm learnings was not a read-output surface at all, so its reads had no output ceiling.

Fix: PM_READ_OUTPUT_TAIL_RETENTION_POLICIES (src/sdk/read-output/continuation.ts) declares comments, notes and learnings as newest-tail paths, as data. Budget compaction and --output-limit retain the tail of those paths. Their continuation cursor carries direction backward: offset counts the older rows still withheld, and replay slices [0, offset) then keeps that slice's newest rows. A cursor whose direction disagrees with the path's declared retention is refused as read_output_cursor_stale. A withheld tail sets total_count beside count, and a producer returned_count is refreshed to the delivered page. learnings joined PM_READ_OUTPUT_SURFACES with --limit as its legacy amount alias.

Measured on this tracker with the built CLI: bare pm comments pm-7zs0 --json now returns indexes 238..263 (count 26, total_count 263), the cursor's next page returns 211..237, and --output-limit 2 returns 262 and 263.

patch.value: On this repository's tracker with the built CLI: bare pm comments pm-7zs0 --json returns indexes 238..263 (count 26, total_count 263, has_more true), following next_cursor returns 211..237, and --output-limit 2 returns 262 and 263 (it returned the two oldest before). tests/unit/sdk/read-output/tail-retention.spec.ts pages comments, notes and learnings backwards to the oldest row in JSON-shaped results. It refuses mismatched-direction cursors and keeps every other surface head-first. The linked tests pass through pm test --run, and so do the focused read-output, annotation and MCP specs (307 tests). Every added source line is covered.

A bare pm comments, notes or learnings read that must be bounded returns the newest entries with total_count beside count and a cursor that continues backwards; --output-limit keeps the newest rows like --limit

PM_READ_OUTPUT_TAIL_RETENTION_POLICIES (src/sdk/read-output/continuation.ts) declares comments, notes and learnings as newest-tail row paths. Budget compaction (compactRowsToBudget) and the --output-limit bound (boundReadOutputRows) retain the tail of those paths instead of the head. The continuation cursor carries direction backward: offset counts the older rows still withheld, and replay slices the collection to them. A cursor issued under the other direction is refused as read_output_cursor_stale. A withheld tail sets total_count beside count, and a producer returned_count is refreshed to the delivered page. learnings joined PM_READ_OUTPUT_SURFACES with --limit as its amount alias, so its reads are bounded like comments and notes. Command reference and read-output contract docs describe the bounded default.
Fixed: bounded comments, notes and learnings reads keep the newest entries and page backwards

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: A universal compaction that always keeps the first rows silently inverts the meaning of a chronological collection: for an append-only log, the head is the least useful part, and the producer's own latest-N limit already disagreed with it. Declare retention per row path as data (PM_READ_OUTPUT_TAIL_RETENTION_POLICIES), make the continuation cursor carry its direction, and refuse a cursor whose direction disagrees with the path's declaration, so pages from the two directions can never be mixed.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 1 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) on PR 1685 found three issues, all verified and fixed. (P1) Adding learnings as a read-output surface without listing its mutation keys in HYBRID_READ_MUTATION_KEYS admitted pm learnings --add/--edit/--delete combined with universal output controls. Before the fix, pm learnings <id> --add x --output-budget 500 wrote the entry (exit 0), and with a stale --output-cursor the write would land before the cursor refusal. learnings now lists add, stdin, file, edit and delete, so the combination is refused before dispatch (exit 2). (P2) attachTailRetentionTotal overwrote a producer total_count with the continuation total. That total describes only the producer's own page (MCP lists 20 comments by default), so a 60-comment item reported total_count 20. An existing producer total is now kept. (P2) A backward replay that needs no further compaction kept the producer count (40 instead of the 26 delivered rows). applyReadOutputContinuation now sets count and returned_count to the delivered slice. Three regression specs in tests/unit/sdk/read-output/tail-retention.spec.ts fail with the two fixed files stashed and pass with them.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 2 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) confirmed the round-1 fixes and found one more reachable P2, verified and fixed. Positional annotation text is a mutation that the read-output guard never saw, because it is not an option key. pm learnings <id> "text" --output-budget 1 appended the entry and then failed the output budget (exit 2), and a retry with the suggested budget appended again. The same bypass existed before this PR for pm comments and pm notes. The preAction validation in src/cli/main.ts now passes annotationPositionalMutationOptions (src/cli/register-annotations.ts), which exposes the text slot of comments, notes and learnings as add. Positional text combined with a universal output control is refused before dispatch for all three commands, through the pm item spelling and the --id form. Reads with an output budget and positional appends without controls are unchanged. tests/unit/cli/annotation-positional-output-controls.spec.ts fails for all three commands with the main.ts wiring stashed.
